service_hints: samba|smbd|netbios|microsoft-ds
SMB → enum4linux-ng -A TARGET; smbclient -L //TARGET -N (null session); connect readable shares and hunt for creds/keys
^ftp|ftp
FTP → anonymous login (nmap --script=ftp-anon TARGET or anonymous:anonymous); writable dirs + config/backup files often hold creds
openssh
SSH → password attack only with a real user list: hydra -L users.txt -P WORDLIST ssh://TARGET
mysql|mariadb
MySQL → default/empty root; hydra mysql TARGET; check remote root and SELECT ... INTO OUTFILE for webshells
microsoft sql server|ms-sql|mssql
MSSQL → hydra mssql TARGET user sa; if in: xp_cmdshell gives command execution
postgres
PostgreSQL → default postgres:postgres; COPY ... FROM PROGRAM gives RCE on ≤11.2 as superuser
wordpress
WordPress → wpscan --url http://TARGET -e ap,u (vulnerable plugins + users); brute wp-login with found users
phpmyadmin
phpMyAdmin → default creds root:root / root:<blank>; check /phpmyadmin/ directly
tomcat|jenkins
Tomcat/Jenkins → manager/console default creds (tomcat:s3cret, admin:admin); WAR/Groovy console = RCE
ldap
LDAP → anonymous bind: ldapsearch -x -H ldap://TARGET -b 'dc=domain,dc=local' — directory dumps leak users and sometimes creds
smtp
SMTP → user enum: nmap --script=smtp-enum-users TARGET (VRFY/EXPN); open relay test
pop3|imap
POP3/IMAP → password spray discovered users: hydra -L users.txt -P WORDLIST TARGET pop3
vnc
VNC → nmap --script=vnc-info TARGET; weak/blank passwords common: medusa -h TARGET -M vnc
rdp|terminal.?services|ms-wbt
RDP → nmap --script=rdp-ntlm-info TARGET leaks domain/host/users (free recon); old Windows → check BlueKeep via nuclei
telnet
Telnet → hydra telnet TARGET; also just connect — unauth shells on embedded/legacy gear are common
nfs|rpcbind
NFS → nmap --script=nfs-ls,nfs-showmount TARGET; mountable exports often expose home dirs/ssh keys
redis
Redis → likely unauth: printf 'INFO\r\n' | nc TARGET 6379; if open, write ssh key via CONFIG SET dir + SAVE
mongodb
MongoDB → nmap --script=mongodb-info,mongodb-databases TARGET; unauth instances are common in the wild
snmp
SNMP → nmap --script=snmp-info TARGET (community 'public'); snmp-brute for weak communities — leaks process/user lists
irc
IRC → connect with nc TARGET 6667; check version (UnrealIRCd backdoor), list channels for info leaks
ajp13
AJP (8009) → Ghostcat CVE-2020-1938 if Tomcat behind it
